newsitem.title: FRANCE: French poll shows PM Juppe's popularity sinks again.
newsitem.headline: French poll shows PM Juppe's popularity sinks again.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe's popularity has sunk again while President Jacques Chirac's standing has risen, an opinion poll published on Wednesday showed.
Pollster CSA said it was the first time the two leaders' ratings had moved apart since the Juppe government was formed in June 1995.
This divergence was likely to draw attention once again to the problem Juppe's deep unpopularity could pose as he leads the conservative majority's election campaign.

Chirac dissolved the National Assembly on April 21 and called a snap two-round parliamentary election for May 25 and June 1. Latest opinion polls show the conservatives winning a sharply reduced majority.

The poll, for La Vie magazine and France Info radio, showed Juppe winning a favourable rating from just 28 percent of those surveyed, matching his all-time low. In March, Juppe's approval rating stood at 30 percent and in February 32 percent.
Sixty-five percent had an unfavourable opinion of the prime minister, compared to 61 percent a month ago.
Chirac's ratings moved in the opposite direction. Forty-one percent expressed support compared to 36 percent in March while 53 percent rated him unfavourably compared to 55 percent in March.
The CSA pollsters questioned 910 people on April 24 and 25.
